newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt posts strong gains, spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt posts strong gains, spreads narrow.

text.p: Emerging markets debt rose solidly as cash that had been sidelined in April continued to roll in, traders and analysts said.
"The whole market is doing pretty well," one trader said. "Today we saw mixed flows all around, and the market has kept its bid."
Brady yield spreads over Treasuries narrowed about 10 to 15 basis points on average, according to traders.
The U.S. interest-rate hike on March 20 and the ensuing uncertainty about monetary policy placed many high-yield allocations on ice.
The recent emerging markets rally can be attributed partially to a rosier outlook on U.S. rates that has allowed for further allocation, traders said.
"A lot of people were not fully invested, and we're closing the gap from where we left off before," another trader said.

Among major Latin issues, Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR rose 1-1/8 to 78-5/8 bid. A late rally followed news the auction of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) had begun, adding to earlier gains, traders said.
Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR were up 1/8 at 93 bid, and Mexico pars MX625L19=RR were up 1/2 at 65-1/2 bid.

Peru posted mixed results during the session, which traders attributed to profit-taking after a sharp rally Monday. Peru PDIs PEPDI=RR were off 3/8 at 62-3/4 bid, while Peru FLIRBs PEFLIRB=RR were up 1/4 at 57-1/2 bid.
Eastern European paper performed well. Russian MinFins climbed between 3/4 and 1-1/4, largely because of expectations for two upcoming Eurobonds, trader said.
"Those gains were mainly in Europe, but they saw a little buying here, too," one trader said.
The City of Moscow plans to issue a three-year, $400 million Eurobond, with a roadshow expected later this month.
Russian U.S. dollar Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were unchanged at 83-1/2 bid, and Bulgaria IABs jumped 1-1/4 to 65-3/8 bid.
